title: The Men Who Left Their Heads In Bed
sources: FBI, 'Alcatraz Escape' (famous cases): on June 12, 1962 John Anglin, Clarence Anglin and Frank Morris were missing; dummy heads of plaster, flesh-tone paint and real human hair in their beds fooled the night guards; raft of more than 50 raincoats

History.com, 'Escape From Alcatraz: June 11, 1962': months digging through cell air vents with sharpened spoons from the cafeteria; dummy heads of paper, soap and human hair from the prison barbershop; raft and life preservers from more than 50 raincoats
Britannica, 'Alcatraz escape of June 1962': night of June 11, 1962; the men were never found

lines.text: In 1962, three men broke out of Alcatraz,
and left their own heads in bed.
See, for months, they dug through the vents in their cells,
with spoons stolen from the canteen.
Every night, the guards counted fake heads
made of soap, paper and real hair.
Then they glued fifty raincoats into a raft,
lines.caps: Then they | glued | 50 | raincoats | into a | raft,

lines.text: The guards found the heads the next morning.
The men were never seen again.
